title: The Hierarchy of Road Users
whatItIs: Since 2022 the Highway Code says that those who can do the greatest harm have the greatest responsibility to look out for others.
keyFacts: The road users most at risk are pedestrians, cyclists, horse riders and motorcyclists.
Children, older people and disabled people are even more at risk.
At a junction, give way to pedestrians crossing or waiting to cross the road you are turning into or out of.
Don't cut across cyclists, horse riders or horse-drawn vehicles going ahead when you turn or change lane.
Everyone still has to take care: the hierarchy doesn't take responsibility away from anyone.

items.title: Rule H1: more harm, more care
items.text: Drivers of larger, faster vehicles have the greatest responsibility to reduce danger to others.

items.title: Rule H2: pedestrians at junctions
items.text: Give way to people crossing or waiting to cross the road you are turning into or out of.

items.title: Rule H2: zebra and parallel crossings
items.text: Give way to pedestrians waiting to cross a zebra, and to people waiting at a parallel crossing.

items.title: Rule H3: don't cut across
items.text: Give way to cyclists and horse riders going ahead when you turn, in a lane, a track or on the road.

b.label: Rule H3
points: When you turn or change lane

onTheTest.question: You are turning left into a side road. A pedestrian is waiting to cross it. What should you do?
options: Give way and let them cross
Turn first, because you have priority
Sound your horn to warn them
onTheTest.why: Rule H2: give way to pedestrians crossing or waiting to cross a road you are turning into. Waving people across can put them in danger.

traps: The hierarchy doesn't mean pedestrians and cyclists can ignore their own safety.
"Waiting to cross" counts, not just people already in the road.
A cyclist going straight on in a cycle lane has priority over you turning across it.
